en.greeting: Hi! Today you write about yourself in English: you, your family and your day, and then a short message or postcard. Let's go step by step.

steps.title: Writing about you
steps.text: Let's start with the sentences you need to write about yourself.
steps.body: You need two things you know. **am / is / are** says who someone is: *I'm a nurse.* The **simple present** says what someone does: *I live in Bandung.* For one other person (he, she, my sister) add **-s**: *my sister lives*; **have** becomes **has**. Never both together: not *I am work*. A good order: **me → my family → my day**.

pairs.en: My father has a small shop.
I get up at six every day.
pairs.id: Aku bangun jam enam setiap hari.

pairs.en: I go to work by bus.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Rina writes about her father. Check the verb.

options: My father work in a hotel.
My father is work in a hotel.
My father works in a hotel.
question.explanation: **My father** = he, one person, so the verb takes **-s**: **works**. *is work* is wrong because am/is/are never goes before another verb.

steps.title: Build the sentence
steps.text: Now write about a mother. Tap the words in order.

question.solution: My mother teaches English at a school.
question.prompt: Arrange the words: Ibu saya mengajar bahasa Inggris di sebuah sekolah.
question.explanation: **My mother** = she, so **teach** takes **-es**: **teaches** (like watch → watches). **English** is a language, so it always has a capital.

steps.title: Capital letters
steps.text: Your sentences are right. Now let's make them look right.
steps.body: Capitals for: the **first word**, **I** (always), **names** (Rina, Pak Hasan), **places** (Bandung), **days** and **months** (Monday, June), **languages** and **nationalities** (English, Indonesian). Most is like Indonesian; the new one is **I**. Jobs (*teacher*), seasons (*summer*) and *my/me* stay small. In chat people type *i live in bandung*; in a message or postcard write **I live in Bandung.**

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Dimas writes about his week in small letters, chat style. Fix it.

question.prompt: Which words need a capital letter? i study english on mondays.
question.explanation: **i** is the first word and always a capital (**I**), **English** is a language and **Mondays** is a day. *study* is a normal verb, so it stays small.

steps.title: One idea, one sentence
steps.text: Next: full stops and commas.
steps.body: End each idea with a **full stop** and start the next with a **capital**. Don't join two sentences with a comma, like *aku tinggal di Medan, kerja di bank* in chat: write two sentences, or join them with **and**. Put a **comma** after the greeting (*Dear Mum,*) and after the ending word (*Love,*) before your name. One **!** sounds friendly; not on every sentence.

pairs.en: I live in Medan. I work in a bank.
pairs.id: Aku tinggal di Medan. Aku bekerja di bank.

pairs.en: I live in Medan and I work in a bank.
pairs.id: Aku tinggal di Medan dan bekerja di bank.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Rina sends a quick message to her friend. Something is wrong.

options: Two sentences are joined with a comma.
question.prompt: Rina writes: 'Hi Sari, I'm at the station, the train is late.' What's the mistake?
question.explanation: *I'm at the station* and *the train is late* are two complete ideas, so they need a **full stop** and a capital: *I'm at the station. The train is late.* *station* is not a name, so it stays small.

steps.title: A postcard from Bali
steps.text: Here's Rina's postcard to her mum, line by line.
steps.body: Three parts: a **greeting**, **2–4 short sentences** (where you are, what it's like, what you do), and an **ending** with your name. **Love,** is for family and close friends; **Best wishes,** is fine for anyone. With all the lines, Rina's card is 35 words: *I'm* counts as one word.

examples.en: The hotel is small but nice.
Every morning we swim in the sea.
examples.id: Setiap pagi kami berenang di laut.

steps.title: Your turn
steps.text: Now a postcard for someone at work.

question.prompt: You write a postcard to your boss, Pak Hasan. Which ending is best?
question.explanation: **Best wishes,** is polite and fine for anyone, also a boss. **Love,** is only for family and close friends, and *Bye bye* is spoken and sounds like a child.

steps.title: Quick review
steps.text: Flip the cards. Say the meaning before you check.

flashcards.back: Kakak perempuanku tinggal di Bogor. (she → lives)

steps.title: Cheat sheet
steps.text: Here's everything on one page. Use it when you write your next message.

artifact.title: Cheat sheet · Writing about yourself
artifact.intro: Sentences about you, capitals, full stops and the parts of a postcard.
rows: am / is / are + who you are
I get up at six every day.
I, Rina, Bandung, Monday, June, English
I live in Medan. I work in a bank.
full stop + capital, not a comma
tips: Check every sentence: **am/is/are** OR another verb, never both (not *I am work*).
Read your text aloud: where your voice stops, put a **full stop**, then a capital.
A message of 25–35 words = greeting + 2–4 short sentences + ending and name.

examples.en: The hotel is small but nice.
Every morning we swim in the sea.
examples.id: Setiap pagi kami berenang di laut.

steps.title: Learn more
steps.text: Want to see more? Here people introduce themselves in short A1 posts.

id.greeting: Hai! Hari ini kamu menulis tentang dirimu dalam bahasa Inggris: dirimu, keluargamu dan harimu, lalu pesan pendek atau kartu pos. Yuk, pelan-pelan saja.

steps.title: Menulis tentang dirimu
steps.text: Kita mulai dengan kalimat yang kamu perlukan untuk menulis tentang dirimu.
steps.body: Kamu butuh dua hal yang sudah kamu kenal. **am / is / are** untuk mengatakan siapa seseorang: *I'm a nurse.* **Simple present** untuk mengatakan apa yang dia lakukan: *I live in Bandung.* Untuk satu orang lain (he, she, my sister) tambahkan **-s**: *my sister lives*; **have** menjadi **has**. Jangan dipakai bersama: bukan *I am work*. Urutan yang enak: **aku → keluargaku → hariku**.

pairs.en: My father has a small shop.
I get up at six every day.
pairs.id: Aku bangun jam enam setiap hari.

pairs.en: I go to work by bus.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Rina menulis tentang ayahnya. Periksa kata kerjanya.

options: My father work in a hotel.
My father is work in a hotel.
My father works in a hotel.
question.explanation: **My father** = he, satu orang, jadi kata kerjanya ditambah **-s**: **works**. *is work* salah karena am/is/are tidak pernah diletakkan sebelum kata kerja lain.

steps.title: Susun kalimatnya
steps.text: Sekarang tulis tentang seorang ibu. Ketuk kata-katanya sesuai urutan.

question.solution: My mother teaches English at a school.
question.prompt: Susun kata-katanya: Ibu saya mengajar bahasa Inggris di sebuah sekolah.
question.explanation: **My mother** = she, jadi **teach** ditambah **-es**: **teaches** (seperti watch → watches). **English** adalah nama bahasa, jadi selalu diawali huruf kapital.

steps.title: Huruf kapital
steps.text: Kalimatmu sudah benar. Sekarang kita buat tulisannya rapi.
steps.body: Huruf kapital untuk: **kata pertama**, **I** (selalu), **nama** (Rina, Pak Hasan), **tempat** (Bandung), **hari** dan **bulan** (Monday, June), **bahasa** dan **kebangsaan** (English, Indonesian). Sebagian besar sama dengan bahasa Indonesia; yang baru adalah **I**. Pekerjaan (*teacher*), musim (*summer*) dan *my/me* tetap huruf kecil. Di chat orang mengetik *i live in bandung*; di pesan atau kartu pos tulis **I live in Bandung.**

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Dimas menulis tentang minggunya dengan huruf kecil semua, gaya chat. Perbaiki.

question.prompt: Kata mana yang perlu huruf kapital? i study english on mondays.
question.explanation: **i** adalah kata pertama dan selalu kapital (**I**), **English** adalah bahasa dan **Mondays** adalah hari. *study* kata kerja biasa, jadi tetap huruf kecil.

steps.title: Satu ide, satu kalimat
steps.text: Berikutnya: titik dan koma.
steps.body: Akhiri setiap ide dengan **titik** (full stop) dan mulai ide berikutnya dengan **huruf kapital**. Jangan gabungkan dua kalimat dengan koma, seperti *aku tinggal di Medan, kerja di bank* di chat: tulis dua kalimat, atau gabungkan dengan **and**. Taruh **koma** setelah salam pembuka (*Dear Mum,*) dan setelah kata penutup (*Love,*) sebelum namamu. Satu **!** terdengar ramah; jangan di setiap kalimat.

pairs.en: I live in Medan. I work in a bank.
pairs.id: Aku tinggal di Medan. Aku bekerja di bank.

pairs.en: I live in Medan and I work in a bank.
pairs.id: Aku tinggal di Medan dan bekerja di bank.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Rina mengirim pesan singkat ke temannya. Ada yang salah.

options: Two sentences are joined with a comma.
question.prompt: Rina menulis: 'Hi Sari, I'm at the station, the train is late.' Apa kesalahannya?
question.explanation: *I'm at the station* dan *the train is late* adalah dua ide lengkap, jadi butuh **titik** dan huruf kapital: *I'm at the station. The train is late.* *station* bukan nama, jadi tetap huruf kecil.

steps.title: Kartu pos dari Bali
steps.text: Ini kartu pos Rina untuk ibunya, baris demi baris.
steps.body: Tiga bagian: **salam pembuka**, **2–4 kalimat pendek** (kamu di mana, tempatnya seperti apa, apa yang kamu lakukan), dan **penutup** dengan namamu. **Love,** untuk keluarga dan sahabat; **Best wishes,** cocok untuk siapa saja. Dengan semua barisnya, kartu Rina berisi 35 kata: *I'm* dihitung satu kata.

examples.en: The hotel is small but nice.
Every morning we swim in the sea.
examples.id: Setiap pagi kami berenang di laut.

steps.title: Giliranmu
steps.text: Sekarang kartu pos untuk orang di kantor.

question.prompt: Kamu menulis kartu pos untuk atasanmu, Pak Hasan. Penutup mana yang paling tepat?
question.explanation: **Best wishes,** sopan dan cocok untuk siapa saja, termasuk atasan. **Love,** hanya untuk keluarga dan sahabat, dan *Bye bye* itu bahasa lisan dan terdengar seperti anak kecil.

steps.title: Ulang cepat
steps.text: Balik kartunya. Sebutkan artinya dulu sebelum mengecek.

flashcards.back: Kakak perempuanku tinggal di Bogor. (she → lives)
